name: Fuyu persimmons
tile_uses: Sliced raw, with cheese, on yogurt
why_now: Fuyus come from North County groves, usually in the last weeks of the month — so don't go looking on the first. When they turn up, they're one of the best things in the store, and almost nobody knows what to do with them.
how_to_choose: Squat and flat on top, shaped like a tomato — that's a Fuyu
Deep orange, with no green near the stem
Tall and acorn-shaped is a Hachiya: leave it until it's soft as jelly
price_note: First of the season costs more. By November they're everywhere and cheap.

flavor_paths.name: Firm and sliced
flavor_paths.description: Crosswise into rounds, no peeling. Like an apple.

flavor_paths.name: With salt
flavor_paths.description: A little olive oil and flaky salt. Sweet against savory.

weekday_uses: Sliced into rounds with pomegranate and a little salt
With cheese, instead of an apple
weekend_use: Sliced thin, dressed with olive oil, salt, and pomegranate, on the table beside the braise.
storage: On the counter until they give very slightly, then the fridge for a week or two.
one_thing_to_learn: The two persimmons in the bin are not interchangeable. A firm Hachiya is so tannic it dries out your whole mouth; it has to go completely soft first. A Fuyu has no such problem and is good crisp. Learn the shape and you'll never make the mistake.
